mmmmm new packages were submitted to CRAN in July. Here are my Top 40 picks in twenty-three categories: Actuarial Analysis, Archaeology, Biology, Causal Inference, Computational Methods, Ecology, Economics, Environmental Studies, Epidemiology, Finance, Functional Data Analysis, Health Technology Assessment, Machine Learning, Medical Statistics, Meta Analysis, Networks, Physics, Programming, Statistics, Time Series, Utilities, and Visualization.

### Causal Inference

[lingamr](https://cran.r-project.org/package=lingamr) v0.1.2: Implements `LiNGAM` (Linear Non-Gaussian Acyclic Model) algorithms for causal discovery, following [Shimizu et al. (2011)](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v12/shimizu11a.html). Based on the `Python` implementation by [Ikeuchi et al. (2023)](https://github.com/cdt15/lingam). The `VAR-LiNGAM` residual diagnostics are inspired by the `VARLiNGAM` `R` code of [Moneta et al.](https://sites.google.com/site/dorisentner/publications/VARLiNGAM). See the [vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lingamr/vignettes/lingamr.html).

![](lingamr.png){fig-alt="Estimated Causal DAG"}

### Climate Studies

[CDSimX](https://cran.r-project.org/package=CDSimX) v1.1.2: Provides advanced climate simulation, forecasting, visualization, export, and machine learning tools. Generates synthetic climate datasets for single or multiple weather stations using stochastic weather generation techniques by simulating daily climate variables including minimum and maximum temperature, rainfall, relative humidity, solar radiation, wind speed, wind direction, dew point temperature, and potential evapotranspiration. Methods are based on established stochastic weather generation approaches described in [Richardson (1981)](https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1029/WR017i001p00182), [Wilks (1999)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0168192399000374?via%3Dihub), and [Osei et al. (2026)](https://openresearchsoftware.metajnl.com/articles/10.5334/jors.666). See the [vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/CDSimX/vignettes/CDSimX-introduction.html).

![](CDSIMX.png){fig-alt="Time series for individual station"}

### Econometrics

[didintrjl](https://cran.r-project.org/package=didintrjl) v0.2.6: Implements a  wrapper for the `Julia` package [`DiDInt.jl`](https://ebjamieson97.github.io/DiDInt.jl/stable/) which implements intersection difference-in-differences (DID-INT), a method developed by [Karim & Webb (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14447). Allows for unbiased estimation of the average effect of treatment on the treated (ATT) in cases when the common causal covariates assumption is violated. Also computes p-values for the ATT via the randomization inference procedure described in MacKinnon and [Webb (2020)]https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304407620301445?via%3Dihub(). See the [vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/didintrjl/vignettes/didintrjl.html).

![](didintrjl.png){fig-alt="Plots of residuals by covariates over time"}

### Geomorphometry

[blueterra](https://cran.r-project.org/package=blueterra) v0.1.0: Derives, organizes, summarizes, and visualizes terrain metrics from bathymetric and elevation rasters for submerged-landscape geomorphometry. Tools support terra-based raster preparation, slope and aspect decomposition, terrain position, rugosity, curvature, depth-band summaries, transect extraction, isobath-corridor analysis, and model-ready summaries for seafloor classification, habitat mapping, shelf-margin analysis, and spatial modeling. Methodological context for geomorphometric terrain analysis is provided by [Lindsay (2016)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0098300416301820?via%3Dihub). There are eight vignettes including [Getting started](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/blueterra/vignettes/blueterra.html) and [Visual proof](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/blueterra/vignettes/visual-proof.html).

![](blueterra.png){fig-alt="Plot of slop over hillside"}

### Mathematics

[riemannianStats](https://cran.r-project.org/package=riemannianStats) v0.2.0: Provides tools for statistical analysis on Riemannian manifolds using local geometry derived from Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP), Isometric Mapping (Isomap), and Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN). The package supports dimensionality reduction, visualization, Riemannian principal component analysis, and Riemannian linear regression for multivariate data analysis. Methods based on Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection follow [McInnes et al. (2018)](https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.00861). There are four vignettes including [Riemannian PCA](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/riemannianStats/vignettes/data10d250-pca-umap-step-by-step.html) and [Riemannian Linear Regression](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/riemannianStats/vignettes/riemannian-regression-umap-dbscan-isomap.html).

![](riemannianStats.png){fig-alt="PCA Biplot"}

### Machine Learning

[modelimportance](https://cran.r-project.org/package=modelimportance) v0.1.0: Provides metrics for quantifying the contribution of individual component models to the predictive accuracy of ensemble forecasts. The package implements the Leave-One-Model-Out and Leave-All-Subset-of-One-Model-Out model importance metrics, enabling users to assess the relative importance of component models and better understand the performance of ensemble forecasting systems. Methods are described in [Kim et al. (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S016920702500127X?via%3Dihub). See the vitnettes [modelimportance](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/modelimportance/vignettes/modelimportance-article.html) and [Simple working examples](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/modelimportance/vignettes/get-started.html).

![](modelimportance.png){fig-alt="Plots showig model importance by task"}

[sdim](https://cran.r-project.org/package=sdim) v0.1.0: Implements five factor extraction methods for asset pricing and macroeconomic forecasting: principal component analysis (PCA), partial least squares (PLS), scaled PCA (sPCA) of [Huang et al. (2022)](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mnsc.2021.4020), the reduced-rank approach (RRA) of [He et al. (2023)](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mnsc.2022.4563), and Instrumented PCA (IPCA) of [Kelly et al. (2019)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0304405X19301151?via%3Dihub). There are four vignettes including [Getting started](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sdim/vignettes/sdim.html) and [Replicating He et al. (2023)](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sdim/vignettes/he2023-table3.html).


### Meta-Analysis

[dtametaTMB](https://cran.r-project.org/package=dtametaTMB) v0.1.1: Fits the hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) model of [Rutter & Gatsonis (2001)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/sim.942), the bivariate binomial-normal model of [Reitsma et al. (2005)](https://www.jclinepi.com/article/S0895-4356(05)00162-9/abstract), the threshold-based bivariate time-to-event model of [Hoyer et al. (2018)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jrsm.1273), and the latent class extensions of [Liu et al. (2015)](https://academic.oup.com/biometrics/article-abstract/71/2/538/7511452?redirectedFrom=fulltext&login=false) for diagnostic studies without a perfect reference standard. Provides subgroup analyses, HSROC meta-regression, likelihood-ratio tests, summary ROC plots, and coupled forest plots. There are three vignettes including [Introduction](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dtametaTMB/vignettes/dtametaTMB.pdf) and [Meta-Regeression](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dtametaTMB/vignettes/Meta-Regression.pdf).

![](dtameta.png){fig-alt="Forest Plot"}

### Networks

[osmnxr](https://cran.r-project.org/package=osmnxr) v0.1.1: Provides a `tidyverse`-friendly toolkit to download, model, simplify, analyze and visualize street networks and other geospatial features from `OpenStreetMap`. Build routable graphs from a place name, address, point or bounding box; simplify topology; compute shortest paths, isochrones and urban metrics (intersection density, circuity, street-orientation entropy, centrality); and export to `sf`, `sfnetworks` and `MapLibr`'. Heavy graph computation is performed by a bundled `Rust` core. There are eight vignettes including [Getting started](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/osmnxr/vignettes/getting-started.html) and [Urban Metrics](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/osmnxr/vignettes/urban-metrics.html).

![](osmnxr.png){fig-alt="Examples of figure-ground diagrams"}

### Utilities

[rtransparency](https://cran.r-project.org/package=rtransparency) v1.0.0; Use this package to identify indicators of transparency within the published literature. It can identify and extract text related to indicators of transparen`cy from specifically formatted `TXT` files and from PMC `XML` files (i.e. `XML files downloaded from the PubMed Central). It builds on the original rtransparent tool of [Serghiou et al. (2021)](https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371/journal.pbio.3001107). There are four vignettes including [Introduction](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rtransparency/vignettes/rtransparency.html) and [Scope and Limitations](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rtransparency/vignettes/scope-and-limitations.html).
